dossier.purpose: Prompt-instruction set for Claude Code: a 7-line root CLAUDE.md plus alternative profiles (profiles/) meant to be copied into a project so Claude answers more tersely, and a stdlib-only Python harness (benchmark/run.py, benchmark/eval.py) that runs `claude -p` with and without a CLAUDE.md to compare output tokens, cost and behavior markers. It is not a context-supply, recoverable-originals or log-based usage-measurement tool. Answer to the need question (single tool that measures provider usage from the local logs Claude Code and Codex write): none in this project. Nothing in the tree reads Claude Code or Codex logs and Codex is never mentioned. run.py takes usage from the live `claude -p --output-format json` result (benchmark/run.py:63-83) and stores input, output, cache-creation and cache-read fields per run in raw JSONL (run.py:72-78), but its reports aggregate only output tokens, words and cost (run.py:108-118, 202-249).

claims.claim: One file, dropped into the project, 'keeps responses terse and can reduce total tokens on output-heavy workflows'.

Instruction files add input tokens on every turn; if the file grows too much it can cost more than it saves. Net is positive only when output volume offsets the persistent input cost; not worth it for short queries, casual use, or many fresh sessions.
Benchmarks were run on Claude only; rules are model-agnostic but local models (llama.cpp, Mistral, others) are untested.
A CLAUDE.md in the project root needs 'one file, zero setup, no code changes' and applies automatically on every message; pasting rules in chat is the no-setup alternative and costs more.

5-prompt benchmark, one run each: 465 words -> 170 words (63% reduction), 'Same information. Zero signal loss.'; self-described as a directional indicator, not a controlled study (no variance controls or repeated runs).

Automated harness (benchmark/): output-token reduction with the current minimal CLAUDE.md is ~4% (haiku), ~12% (sonnet), ~7% (opus); the 63% figure is 'achievable with a stricter rules profile' via `python3 benchmark/run.py -n 5 --model opus`.
Semantic eval confirms baselines on current models already show 0% preamble, sycophancy, 'as an AI' and smart quotes, so rules targeting those carry input cost without changing output.

An independent third-party benchmark (adam-s/testing-claude-agent) ran 6 configs on 3 coding challenges, all passing, so comparison was cost-to-green; the project's own v8 config beat C-structured $0.935 vs $1.131 (-17.4%).
Root CLAUDE.md is kept to a small set of high-impact rules to minimize recurring input overhead.
At scale: ~9,600 tokens/day (~$0.86/month on Sonnet) saved at 100 prompts/day; ~96,000 tokens/day (~$8.64) at 1,000 prompts/day.
The root file fixes eight behaviors, including targeted edits, running tests before finishing, simple fixes, and 'user instructions always override'.
Three versioned sets with tool budgets: J-drona23-v5 50 calls, K-drona23-v6 50 calls, M-drona23-v8 20 calls; the v8 config 'uses 2 files (7 lines total)'.
A CLAUDE.md file is 'cached efficiently'; rules pasted in chat cost +41% vs CLAUDE.md v8 ($1.318 vs $0.935 over 3 coding challenges).
Third-party browser tools (Token Checkup, Cache Health Checker) analyze token use or cache efficiency from pasted /cost output.

code.architecture: No runtime library or service. Content: root CLAUDE.md (6 rule bullets) and RULES.md; profiles/ holds five single-file profiles and three multi-file sets (rules/, agents/, reference/ subfolders, each set's CLAUDE.md being a one-line pointer to .claude/ paths). Measurement: benchmark/run.py builds a condition x prompt x run grid (5 fixed one-shot Q&A prompts, run.py:38-44), runs each in a fresh temp dir via subprocess `claude -p ... --output-format json --setting-sources project` on a ThreadPoolExecutor (default 3 workers), retries with backoff, appends one JSON line per run to raw-<model>.jsonl (output_tokens, words, cost, input and cache tokens, num_turns, duration_ms, session_id, result_text; run.py:70-83), then writes report-<model>.md with per-prompt means (run.py:108-118, 202-249). benchmark/eval.py reads those raw files, applies regex markers (preamble, sycophancy, closing fluff, 'as an AI', em-dash, smart quotes; eval.py:51-79) and a Haiku judge also run through `claude -p` (eval.py:85-121), and writes SEMANTIC.md for the 'baseline' and 'CLAUDE.md' conditions only (eval.py:175). Committed results: benchmark/SUMMARY.md, SEMANTIC.md, report-*.md, raw-*.jsonl. BENCHMARK.md (headed 'Project: PromptOS', 2026-03-30) and examples/before-after.md are narrative/illustrative documents (examples/before-after.md:2).

risks: Scope gap for the stated need: no log-based usage measurement, no Codex support, no context-supply or recoverable-originals mechanism. Nothing reads Claude Code or Codex local logs (searches for ~/.claude/projects, .codex, codex found only an unrelated ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md mention at README.md:171). The harness takes usage from live `claude -p` output (benchmark/run.py:52-83), stores input and cache fields (run.py:76-78) but reports only output tokens, words and cost (run.py:108-118, 202-249).

Headline claims are not supported by the repo's own data, and the narrative text is inconsistent: README.md:94 percentages differ from benchmark/SUMMARY.md:14-16; the 63% figure does not reproduce on the current file (SUMMARY.md:34); SUMMARY.md:35 labels -11% as opus although its table shows -11% for sonnet and -7% for opus; SUMMARY.md:37 calls opus 'the chattiest baseline' although haiku has the highest baseline output tokens in its table (2266 vs 1888).

Weak, hard-to-tie measurement: 5 one-shot Q&A prompts (run.py:38-44), N=5, means only with no variance or significance (run.py:108-118); per-cell ranges overlap (haiku T1 output tokens baseline 614-783 vs CLAUDE.md 595-745 in raw-haiku.jsonl); agentic/coding loops are not measured (SUMMARY.md:46). Raw records store `claude_md` as a maintainer-local path ('<private>'), not a content hash (run.py:169), and SEMANTIC.md:55 / eval.py:210-212 say the file has no em-dash rule while the current CLAUDE.md:6 does, so either the file changed after capture or the text is stale and the data cannot say which.

Net effect is small or negative for low-output work, and the largest savings come from a profile that removes guards: the minimal file adds about 190-310 cache-creation input tokens per call in the raw data, with cost change haiku +1.9%, sonnet -0.6% (report-*.md:16-17); README.md:4, 72 concede this. profiles/CLAUDE.compressed.md:17 and SUMMARY.md:30 say the stricter profile drops fabrication and re-read guards, with no correctness eval on it. v8 caps work at 20 tool calls (profiles/M-drona23-v8/rules/workflow.md:3).

Unpinned, unsigned distribution of standing instructions: README.md:237 downloads CLAUDE.md from the main branch with curl; there are no tags, releases, checksums or signatures in the tree. The file is loaded as instructions on every message (README.md:36-41), so any upstream edit changes agent behavior without review.

Undocumented side-effect hook: .claude/settings.json:3-12 runs `git add -A` and then `git commit --no-verify` on every PreCompact when changes are staged (stderr suppressed, `|| true`), committing the whole working tree. README never mentions the file or hook; it applies if the clone is opened in Claude Code or the .claude directory is copied.

Profiles are tuned to the benchmark tasks and under-documented: v6 and v8 hard-code WebSocket guidance (Set, setTimeout(0), no pub/sub) and 'read the test file first' (profiles/M-drona23-v8/rules/workflow.md:5, 10; profiles/K-drona23-v6/reference/patterns.md:8, 15); README lists K-v6 at 50 tool calls but the file says 30 (README.md:200 vs profiles/K-drona23-v6/agents/builder.md:6); no install steps for the multi-file sets; README's profile table omits CLAUDE.compressed.md and RULES.md (README.md:185-191); benchmark/CLAUDE.md:17 uses a '../' --variant path that run.py:138 would resolve outside the repo (read, not run).

Maintenance and verification limits: no tests, CI, releases or security policy (no .github directory, no SECURITY file); single named maintainer (LICENSE:3); the shallow clone holds one commit so history and activity cannot be assessed here; Python 3.10+ is implied but undocumented (run.py:47). Running the harness needs a logged-in `claude` CLI and spends quota (50 benchmark calls per model at N=5 plus one judge call per record, run.py:160-163, eval.py:153-161) and is tuned to 3 workers to avoid rate limits (run.py:130).
